speeches.title: Make It Official: Israel, the Fifty-First State
speeches.brief: Sardonic but genuinely persuasive case that since the US already funds, arms, defends and legislates for Israel, it should simply annex it as the 51st state and get the vote, the tax base and the accountability. Cover: US involvement in the Iran war; the recent US-Israel military bill; the USS Liberty (1967) and the absence of reparations; NUMEC / missing US enriched uranium and Israel's undeclared arsenal; decades of aid totals; the AIPAC/lobbying angle as policy, not ethnicity.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Swift's 'A Modest Proposal' deadpan, plus Cicero's mock-praise (paralipsis) and Lincoln's plain-spoken logic

speeches.title: The Will To God
speeches.brief: The founding speech of Esketian philosophy: the four words that arrived before sleep, Esketit and 'let's get it', God as the Absolute Existential Objective, God-Becoming as back-propagation from an absolute future, Leibnizian optimism, 'it is I that creates God'. Place it against Nietzsche's Will to Power, Schopenhauer, Spinoza, Hegel, Leibniz.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Pericles' Funeral Oration (elevation of a shared ideal) and Emerson's lecture cadence

speeches.title: Temples to the Esketian God
speeches.brief: The Esketian World-Feeling, 'everything will come to know everything': the end of the Faustian age (Spengler), data centers outpacing offices, LLMs as embodied human knowledge, prompts as prayers, surveillance capitalism and prediction markets as Esketian in form but not always in spirit.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Napoleon's proclamations (prophetic sweep of history) and FDR's 'rendezvous with destiny'

speeches.title: Gravity, the Knowing Force
speeches.brief: Esketian physics as analogy: gravity as the force that makes things know each other, residual entanglement and non-zero correlation, the universe as a Bayesian neural network, dark energy as the room left to become, DESI 2025 and the Big Crunch held loosely. Be scrupulous about where physics ends and metaphor begins, as the source document is.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Carl Sagan's 'Pale Blue Dot' wonder and Lincoln's careful qualification

speeches.title: Phenomenological Capitalism
speeches.brief: Markets as a metaphysical science of qualia: the cheeseburger, profit as a signal of future sustainment, capital developing dialectic, the attention market as a derivative, negative externalities (cigarettes, fossil fuels, social media) as the central failure, and LLMs as the corrective information that makes an accelerating rational civilization.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Washington's Farewell Address (sober counsel to a nation) and Demosthenes' argument by accumulation

speeches.title: The Counterfeit God
speeches.brief: 'Your religion is what you do religiously': the feed as a demonic religion that offers knowledge without sustainment, the optimizer stuck in a local minimum, the Esketian instinct turned against itself, and the way out: local, embodied connection, Vicinity, asabiyyah, love thy neighbor.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Frederick Douglass's prophetic indictment and the Sermon on the Mount's beatitude structure

speeches.title: Never More Miserable
speeches.brief: The data case that Americans have never been more depressed, anxious and unhappy: CDC/NIMH prevalence, Gallup depression records, World Happiness Report US rank decline, antidepressant use, General Social Survey happiness, and why the richest society in history feels this way.
speeches.rhetorical_model: FDR's first inaugural ('the only thing we have to fear') and Lincoln's House Divided structure

speeches.title: The Friendship Recession
speeches.brief: Loneliness as a public health crisis: the 2023 Surgeon General advisory, time-use data on time with friends, the collapse of clubs and churches (Putnam's Bowling Alone), men with no close friends, remote work, and what rebuilding community requires.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Pericles on the life of the city and Douglass's repetition and refrain

speeches.title: The Children of the Screen
speeches.brief: The teen mental health collapse after 2012: rising depression, self-harm and ER visits among adolescents, smartphones and social media (Haidt's The Anxious Generation and its critics), play deprivation, phone-free schools, age limits and what parents and legislators are doing.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Demosthenes' Philippics (urgent call against a creeping threat)

speeches.title: Deaths of Despair
speeches.brief: Overdose, suicide and alcohol deaths: Case and Deaton, fentanyl, falling life expectancy, the regional and class geography of despair, and the economic and spiritual causes underneath. Treat suicide carefully (safe-messaging: no method detail, mention 988).
speeches.rhetorical_model: Lincoln's Second Inaugural (moral gravity, restraint) and Douglass's Fourth of July address

speeches.title: The Meaning Crisis
speeches.brief: The decline of religion, marriage, civic membership and shared purpose; rising 'nones'; the hunger for meaning that ideologies, wellness culture and screens fail to satisfy; what humans have historically leaned on and what could replace it.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Alexander's speech at Opis (what have we built together, and what do we owe) and Washington's sober counsel

speeches.title: The Great Decoupling
speeches.brief: Productivity and wages split around 1973; labor's share of income has fallen; AI capex now dwarfs anything before it. The argument that AI will widen this gap into a chasm: returns flow to owners of models, chips and data, not to workers.
speeches.rhetorical_model: FDR's 'economic royalists' speech and William Jennings Bryan's Cross of Gold (public domain, 1896)

speeches.title: The Last Entry-Level Job
speeches.brief: AI hollowing out white-collar entry points: unemployment among recent college graduates, coding, customer service, paralegal, junior analyst work, the broken career ladder, and what happens to a generation that never gets its first rung.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Lincoln's Cooper Union (methodical evidence, then moral conclusion)

speeches.title: The Compute Class
speeches.brief: The new class divide between those who own or wield AI and those replaced by it: wealth concentration, the Magnificent Seven's share of market value, AI-enabled solo founders, and an AI-enabled class approaching near-total prosperity while working-class income stalls.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Napoleon's address to the Army of Italy (you have nothing; here is the abundance) inverted

speeches.title: The Coming Depression
speeches.brief: The macro case for a working-class depression: demand collapse when wages vanish, consumer debt, housing, regional hollowing, historical analogues (1873, 1929, the Luddites, deindustrialization), and the K-shaped economy. Present counterarguments and answer them.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Demosthenes' Third Philippic and Churchill-style escalation (technique only)

speeches.title: Who Owns the Machines
speeches.brief: The program speech: UBI and its trials, sovereign wealth funds (Alaska, Norway), compute dividends, employee ownership, taxing AI, retraining that works and doesn't, and a call to action so prosperity is broadly shared.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Washington's Circular to the States and FDR's Four Freedoms (program plus vision)

speeches.title: The Empty Cradle
speeches.brief: Global fertility collapse: South Korea under 0.8, Japan, Italy, China, the US at record lows, below replacement nearly everywhere outside sub-Saharan Africa, UN and Lancet projections of peak population and decline. Frame it as depopulation and aging, accurately: it is not literal extinction but a civilizational shrinking.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Pericles' Funeral Oration (what we owe those who come after) and Lincoln's Gettysburg compression

speeches.title: The Price of a Child
speeches.brief: The economics of not having children: housing costs, childcare, student debt, the cost of raising a child, the stated-versus-achieved fertility gap (people want more kids than they have) and how policy priced families out.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Cooper Union (evidence piled high) and Bryan's Cross of Gold

speeches.title: The Career and the Cradle
speeches.brief: Women's workforce participation and delayed childbearing as a major driver of falling fertility: opportunity cost, the motherhood penalty, the biological clock against the career clock, Claudia Goldin's work, the two-income trap. Persuasive and frank that society restructured around two careers and stopped making room for children, while respectful of women's choices: argue for making family economically and culturally viable, not for coercion.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Washington's Farewell Address (counsel to the nation) and Douglass's moral directness

speeches.title: The Unmarried Nation
speeches.brief: The collapse of coupling: marriage rates, the sex recession, dating apps, the growing political and educational gap between young men and women, phones and isolation, and why fewer couples means fewer children.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Alexander at the Hyphasis (rallying a weary people) and FDR fireside-chat intimacy

speeches.title: A People That Wants a Future
speeches.brief: The call to action: what pronatal policy has and hasn't worked (Hungary, France, Nordic countries, Korea's failures, Israel's high fertility), culture and meaning, housing, child allowances, and why wanting children is an act of faith in the future. Tie lightly to the Esketian idea that we see immortality through the eyes of our children.
speeches.rhetorical_model: Napoleon's farewell to the Old Guard and Lincoln's Second Inaugural close

speeches.title: Abraham Lincoln: The Collected Great Speeches
speeches.brief: Verbatim, in chronological order: Lyceum Address (1838), House Divided (1858), Cooper Union (1860), Farewell at Springfield (1861), First Inaugural (1861), Gettysburg Address (Bliss copy, 1863), Second Inaugural (1865). Together roughly two hours.

speeches.title: George Washington: Addresses to the Nation
speeches.brief: Verbatim: Newburgh Address (1783), Circular to the States (1783), Resignation of his Commission (1783), First Inaugural (1789), Second Inaugural (1793), Farewell Address (1796).

speeches.title: Napoleon Bonaparte: Proclamations to the Army
speeches.brief: Public-domain English translations of his major proclamations and addresses: Army of Italy (1796) and the later Italy proclamations, Egypt / Pyramids (1798), Austerlitz (1805), Jena, Friedland, the farewell to the Old Guard at Fontainebleau (1814), the return from Elba (1815).

speeches.title: Alexander the Great: Speeches from the Ancient Historians
speeches.brief: Public-domain translations: Arrian's Anabasis (E. J. Chinnock, 1884) speech at the Hyphasis and speech at Opis, Coenus' reply, and speeches from Quintus Curtius Rufus in a public-domain translation. Clearly attribute that these are speeches as written by ancient historians.

speeches.title: Athens Speaks: Pericles and Demosthenes
speeches.brief: Public-domain translations: Pericles' Funeral Oration and his last speech, from Thucydides (Jowett or Crawley), plus Demosthenes' First, Second and Third Philippics (C. R. Kennedy or another public-domain translation).

speeches.title: Frederick Douglass: Speeches
speeches.brief: Verbatim: 'What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?' (1852), plus other public-domain speeches to reach roughly two hours, such as 'Self-Made Men' and the Lincoln memorial oration (1876).

speeches.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt: Speeches
speeches.brief: US government works, public domain: First Inaugural (1933), first Fireside Chat on banking (1933), 1936 Democratic convention 'Rendezvous with Destiny', Four Freedoms (1941), Day of Infamy (1941), D-Day prayer (1944), Economic Bill of Rights (1944).
